newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks close higher, led by foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks close higher, led by foreigners.

text.p: Late foreign buying helped Sri Lankan stocks close higher on Wednesday, brokers said.
The all share index closed at 564.70, up 2.4 points.
"While foreigners bought expensive stocks, local retailers were getting in among the cheap shares," said Tivanka Ratnayake of brokerage John Keells.
Gainers led decliners by 25 to 12. Commercial Bank rose 1.75 to 92 rupees, Development Finance 1.50 to 266.50 and JKH 50 cents to 172.50.
Plantation shares were a favourite among retail investors, he said.
Plantation companies Bogowantalawa rose 3.50 rupees to 22 rupees, Agalawatte 25 cents to 22 rupees and Kelani Valley 75 cents to 22.75 rupees.
Tea Smallholder Factories which process leaf provided by small-scale cultivators, rose 50 cents to 18.50.
"Retailers are encouraged by the foreign buying they saw in the past few days. They expect it to result in an overall upward movement which would help them to take some profit," said Ratnayake.
Turnover was an active 36.09 million rupees.
